medicus, medicī m.

noun, second declension

Other words

  • medica, medicae f. — doctor (woman)

    noun, first declension · classical · Traupman 166; Traupman 63; M-O s.v. doctor

Examples

  • Medicus aurēs tuās īnspiciet; nihil dolēbit.

    The doctor will look in your ears; it won’t hurt.composed

  • medicum arcessere

    send for the doctorPlaut. Men. 875 (Lewis & Short)

  • Vīse medicum quam prīmum

    see a doctor as soon as possible (said to Traupman’s sick girl)Traupman 55

  • Hodiē ad medicum īmus.

    We’re going to the doctor today.composed

  • Medicus tē īnspiciet: ōs aperī, linguam exsere.

    The doctor will look at you: open your mouth, stick out your tongue.composed

See also dentist, nurse, hospital, doctor’s surgery, pharmacist, examine, medicine.
